rationale:
The linked issue (apple/swift-openapi-generator#251, 'URLSession and AHC transports double-encode path parameters', closed) names exactly the defect the one-line production change addresses: assigning an already percent-encoded request path to URLComponents.path re-encodes '%' as '%25', so the fix switches to percentEncodedPath. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in Sources/OpenAPIURLSession/URLSessionTransport.swift changing only that assignment; no refactor, formatting, feature, doc, or config edits, and post-minimization validation is PASS with retained_hunks=[1], removed=0. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test portion of the same fixing commit: testRequestConversion now sends path '/hello%20world/Maria' and asserts the resulting URL keeps '%20'. Both the test API (OpenAPIRuntime.Request, URLRequest(_:baseURL:)) and the Foundation URLComponents members already exist on the buggy revision, so this is a genuine behavioral differential rather than a fix-only-API compile error: on the buggy revision the URL becomes '.../hello%2520world/Maria' and the assertion fails. Strict machine evidence confirms build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproduced on Tests/OpenAPIURLSessionTests/URLSessionTransportTests.swift::testRequestConversion, trigger.fixed_clean PASS, trigger.deterministic across 3 repetitions, and full_suite.fixed_all_green with no failed checks in either strict_original or strict_post_minimization. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so the root cause is not a duplicate, and the id matches the single entry in allowed_root_cause_ids.

Linked issue apple/swift-openapi-generator#251 reports that the URLSession transport double-encodes path parameters. The minimized production patch is the single line `baseUrlComponents.path += request.path` -> `baseUrlComponents.percentEncodedPath += request.path` in URLSessionTransport.swift, which is precisely the double-encoding root cause: assigning to `path` re-percent-encodes an already-encoded path from the generated client, turning `%20` into `%2520`. The upstream trigger, testRequestConversion, changes only the fixture path to `/hello%20world/Maria` and the expected URL to `http://example.com/api/hello%20world/Maria?greeting=Howdy`, so it observes exactly the reported symptom rather than a new feature. The trigger uses only pre-existing client API (OpenAPIRuntime.Request, URLRequest(_:baseURL:)) and no fix-only symbol, so the same test source compiles and runs on both revisions; strict evidence records build.both_versions PASS, an isolated buggy differential failure on the declared selector, deterministic outcomes across 3 repetitions, buggy full-suite failures limited to the reproduced trigger, and fixed all-green, both pre- and post-minimization. The patch contains no refactor, formatting, docs, config, or test-only content (original_hunk_count 1, retained 1, removed 0; post_minimization_validation PASS). The active same-project root-cause registry is empty, so this URL path double-encoding cause is not a duplicate, and the id matches the sole allowed key.
